title: Automated Contraction Analysis of Human Engineered Heart Tissue for Cardiac Drug Safety Screening
protocol: Coat 6-well plates or T75 flasks with reduced growth factor basement membrane matrix diluted in DMEM for 30 min at 37 °C.
Prepare FTDA medium by mixing basic DMEM/F-12 medium with specified components.
Seed hiPSC (~3 x 10^5/ 10 cm²) in FTDA medium and culture at 37 °C, 5% CO₂, 21% O₂ with daily medium change.
Passage hiPSC (1:2-1:6) with EDTA for ~4 min.
Wash confluent flasks twice with PBS without calcium and magnesium.
Incubate cells in 0.5 mM EDTA for ~10 min.
Remove EDTA from the flask using a glass pipette.
Flush off cells with 10 mL PBS, tapping flasks at the bench to detach cells.
Use cell scraper if necessary to ensure complete detachment of cells.
Collect cells in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add one-quarter of the volume of RPMI 1640 medium to the cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 250 x g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cell pellet in FTDA medium supplemented with 4 mg/mL polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and 10 µM Y-27632.
Count the cells in a Neubauer chamber.
Fill the spinner flask with the cell suspension at a concentration of 30 x 10^6 cells per 100 mL FTDA medium supplemented with PVA and Y-27632.
Initiate EB formation in spinner flasks by adjusting the rotor speed to 40 rpm.
Culture the EBs overnight at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 5% O2.
Coat cell culture flasks suitable for suspension culture with non-ionic surfactant overnight at 37 °C.
The next morning, wash the surfactant-coated flasks twice with PBS.
Add PBS again to the flasks and keep them in the incubator until needed.
Remove the spinner flask from the incubator.
Transfer 50 mL of suspension to a 50 mL conical tube.
Let EBs settle for 5-20 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 7 mL of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 2% PVA and 10 µM Y-27632.
Transfer the suspension to a graduated 15 mL conical tube.
Estimate EB volume (~50-100 µL).
Transfer contents of the spinner flasks to uncoated T175 flasks.
Leave T175 flask on V-shaped rack for sedimentation up to 20 min.
Remove supernatant from T175 flask.
Wash embryoid bodies as stated above.
Split EB suspension into several T175 flasks if initial spinner flask volume exceeds 200 mL.
Combine EBs after washing.
Resuspend washed EBs in medium for mesodermal differentiation, which includes RPMI supplemented with specified additives.
Remove PBS from surfactant-coated T175 flasks.
Fill surfactant-coated T175 flasks with cell suspension (200 μL EBs in 40 mL).
Cultivate EBs in suspension for three days under specified conditions.
Exchange 50% of the medium every day using V-shaped sedimentation rack.
Prepare fresh medium prior to feeding each day.
Let EBs settle on a sedimentation rack for up to 5 minutes after three days of mesodermal induction.
Remove most of the medium from the settled EBs.
Wash EBs with RPMI 1640 supplemented with 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin and 10 mM HEPES.
Transfer 10 mL of EB suspension to a graduated 15 mL tube.
Estimate the volume of EBs after sedimentation in the tube.

Resuspend EBs carefully in cardiac differentiation medium consisting of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin, 10 mM HEPES, 0.05% human serum albumin, 5 µg/mL transferrin, 5 ng/mL sodium selenite, 0.1% lipid mix, 250 µM phospho-ascorbate, 1 µM Y-27632, and 100 nM Wnt-inhibitor DS-I-713.
Transfer EBs to new surfactant-coated cell culture flasks (about 200 μL of EBs in 46 mL/T175).
Incubate for three days at 37 °C, 5% CO₂, and 21% O₂ with a 50% medium change on the second and third day.
Do not change the medium within the first 48 hours.

After three days, incubate EBs in medium consisting of RPMI 1640 supplemented with 500 µM 1-Thioglycerol, 10 mM HEPES, 0.5% penicillin/streptomycin, 1 µM Y-27632, and 2% serum-free neural cell culture supplement (e.g., B27) with insulin, plus 100 nM Wnt-inhibitor DS-I-7.
Change 50% of the medium daily for the next four days except on the first day.
Switch to the same medium without Wnt inhibition and with serum-free neural cell culture supplement after one week of cardiac differentiation.
Continue changing 50% of the medium every day, excluding the first day.
Weigh and dissolve collagenase to make a solution at 200 U/mL in calcium-free Hanks' balanced salt solution without Ca/Mg (HBSS).
Add 1 mM HEPES, 10 µM Y-27632, and 30 µM BTS to the collagenase solution.
Sterilize the collagenase solution by filtering it through a 0.2 μm filter.
Store sterilized collagenase aliquots at -20 °C.
Thaw collagenase aliquots overnight at 4 °C.
Settle EBs on sedimentation racks, aspirate medium, and replace with pre-warmed HBSS (20-25 ml).
Repeat the washing step once more using pre-warmed HBSS.
Aspirate the HBSS and replace with pre-warmed collagenase solution (15 ml/T175).
Incubate for 4 h in a cell culture incubator at 37 °C, 5% CO2, and 21% O2.
Prepare blocking buffer by supplementing DMEM with penicillin/streptomycin and DNase (12 µg/mL).
Tap the flasks gently on the bench to dissociate EBs further if necessary increase incubation time.
Transfer the cell suspension to a conical 50 ml tube after gentle trituration.
Wash the flasks with blocking buffer (15 ml/T175) and transfer the wash to the tube.
Centrifuge cells for 10 min at 100 x g.
Resuspend cells in warm DMEM, triturate, and count cells.
Autoclave commercially available PDMS racks and polytetrafluorethylene spacers.
Weigh and dissolve appropriate amount of agarose in PBS to prepare a 2% solution under sterile conditions.
Autoclave the prepared 2% agarose solution and immediately store at 60 °C.
Weigh and dissolve aprotinin in aqua ad iniectabilia, then filter sterilize through a 0.22-µm filter.
Aliquot filtered aprotinin and store at -20 °C.
Dissolve sterile fibrinogen in an appropriate volume of sterile 0.9% NaCl solution.
Aliquot the dissolved fibrinogen and store at -20 °C.
Mix three parts sterile PBS with two parts aqua ad iniectabilia to dissolve thrombin.
Aliquot portions of 3 µL of the dissolved thrombin and store at -20 °C.
Dissolve 670 mg 10x DMEM powder in 5 mL aqua ad iniectabilia under sterile conditions.
Filter sterilize the prepared 10x DMEM solution and store at 4 °C.
Mix 2 mL of 10x DMEM with 2 mL heat-inactivated horse serum, 0.2 mL penicillin/streptomycin, and 5.8 mL aqua ad iniectabilia under sterile conditions.
Filter sterilize the mixture and store the prepared 2x DMEM at 4 °C.
Mix DMEM with 10% heat-inactivated fetal calf serum, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 1% L-glutamine to prepare ECM.
Store ECM at 4 °C.
Pipette 1.6 mL of warm agarose (2%, PBS) into each well of a 24-well plate.
Place the PTFE spacer in each well to create casting molds.
Prepare the reconstitution mix in a round bottom 15-mL tube on ice.
Add ECM and cells to the reconstitution mix according to species requirements (human, rat, or mouse).
Adjust volume of cell suspension to a final volume of 2,640 µL with additional ECM if necessary.
Warm fibrinogen to lukewarm temperature before pipetting.
Slowly fill the tip of the pipette and avoid touching cold reconstitution mix when adding fibrinogen.
Triturate the reconstitution mix 10 - 15 times with a serological pipette until fibrinogen clot is dissolved.
Pipette 100 µL reconstitution mix into one thrombin aliquot (3 µL in 200 µL tube).
Mix the mixture thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture into the agarose-slots as quickly as possible.
Resuspend the reconstitution mix by trituration with a serological pipette after every 8 EHTs using new filter tips for each EHT.
Close the lid of the cell culture dish and incubate at 37 °C, 7% CO2 for 2 h.
Remove the plate from the incubator.
Place the plate under a sterile hood.
Cover each well with approximately 200 - 500 µL of medium (e.g., DMEM).
Shake the plate gently and reincubate at 37 °C for at least 10 min.

Prepare a new 24-well plate with 1.5 mL EHT-medium per well consisting of DMEM supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated horse serum, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, 10 µg/mL insulin, and 33 µg/mL aprotinin.
Carefully remove the PDMS racks from the agarose casting molds.
Transfer them to the medium-filled 24-well plate.
Place the dish back in the incubator (37 °C, 7% CO2, 40% O2 for human and rat EHTs; 21% O2 for mouse EHTs).
Feed the cultures with freshly prepared EHT-medium Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.
Turn on the heating device of the EHT analysis machine 2 h prior to measurement.
Turn on gas supply and electronic supply of the axis system immediately before contraction analysis.
Place the 24-well-plate with EHTs in EHT-medium into the instrument for baseline recording.
Start the contraction analysis software according to supplier manual.
Enter relevant information regarding study name, user, species, cell type, age, recording length and additional remarks in the "Protocol" tab.
Click the "Camera view" tab and start camera live mode with automatic figure detection mode.
Adjust the camera position with xyz coordinates for each well in the 24-well-dish on the "Setup" tab.
Ensure the lid of the cell culture dish is not foggy to maintain figure recognition accuracy.
Save setup positions of each well by pressing "position ok".
Click the "Parameters" tab in the software to adjust criteria for contraction peak identification.
Set parameters accurately to avoid false data points during contraction analysis.
Click the "Automatic" tab on the right panel.
Initiate the analysis by activating the "Start" button.
Save and analyze the pdf report generated to summarize the results.
Monitor the contractile parameters by repeated measurement over several days.
Prepare protein-free Tyrode solution one day prior to measurement.
Equilibrate in 24-well plates (2 mL/well) in the cell culture incubator overnight.
Add calcium up to 1.8 mM or the previously determined [EC50] to investigate positive inotropic effects.
Weigh and dissolve the drug in DMSO.
Filter sterile, if necessary.
Prepare 6 different 1000x-sub-stock solutions (in DMSO) of the working concentration.
Dilute the respective stock in the Tyrode plates (2 µL in each 2 mL well).
Mix thoroughly.
Place the plates back in the incubator until needed.
Take the first Tyrode-filled 24-well-plate under the sterile hood.
Position carbon electrodes in the wells.
Transfer PDMS racks with EHTs onto carbon electrodes, close lid, and place plate back in incubator for ~30 min equilibration period.
Transfer EHTs from incubator to interlock in EHT analysis instrument.
Close instrument and record spontaneous baseline contractility (20 s/EHT).
Connect carbon electrodes to pacing cable.
Start electrical stimulation of EHTs (2.5 V, 4 ms impulse duration, human: ~1 Hz, rat: ~2 Hz, mouse: ~4 Hz).
Record "paced" baseline (10 s/EHT).
Ensure all EHTs are properly paced.
Remove EHTs from instrument and transfer electrodes with PDMS racks to 24-well-plate with first drug concentration.
Transfer EHTs back onto interlock of EHT analysis instrument immediately for incubation (e.g., 20 min).
Reconnect pacing cables, adjust figure recognition, and record EHT contractions responding to the first drug concentration.
For higher drug concentrations, repeat steps involving transfer, reconnection, and recording.
Save all pdf recordings.
Check each recording for figure recognition.
Correct positioning of green squares identifying contraction peaks and artifacts.
Perform additional offline analysis if needed.
Select the respective run from the "Runs" database on the left panel by clicking "Select run".
Change parameters for contraction analysis in the "Parameter" tab on the left.
Choose "Offline analysis" in the "Offline" tab on the right panel to reanalyze the videos.
Adjust figure recognition and record a new video file using "Sample review" after adjusting the figure recognition in the "Real time" tab.
Use parameter on all wells by clicking the button "Use parameter on all wells" in the "Parameter" panel on the left for offline analysis of multiple wells.
Analyze the experiment by combining the results of the biological replicates.
Summarize the data in concentration response curves for frequency, contraction force, contraction time and relaxation time.
Display graphical representation of average contraction peaks.
